title: Lightweight Federated Learning for Efficient Network Intrusion Detection
researchArea: Cyber Security, Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS), Federated Learning (FL), Deep Learning (CNNs), Structured Model Pruning, Resource-Constrained Edge Security
problem: Traditional Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) face high computational and storage costs, high latency, energy-intensive training, and data privacy risks when raw network traffic is centralized. Standard FL mitigates data privacy concerns, but training large deep learning architectures (e.g., CNNs) across distributed, resource-constrained edge devices creates computational bottlenecks and high communication overhead.
motivation: Protecting modern interconnected network infrastructure against malicious cyberattacks (such as zero-day threats and DDoS) without centralized raw traffic collection. Integrating zero-shot structured pruning with FL reduces model size, memory usage, FLOPs, and communication overhead while preserving data privacy (GDPR/privacy-compliant) and high detection accuracy on edge devices.
noveltyAndContributions: Proposed Lightweight-Fed-NIDS, combining Federated Learning (FL) with a data-free (zero-shot) structured pruning technique (DepGraph dependency graph criteria)
Computed a one-time pruning mask at the global server without accessing client data, broadcasting it once during initialization
Used deep CNN feature extractors (ResNet-50, ResNet-101, VGG-19) on 3-channel image representations of raw network flows (300 bytes × 40 packets)
Evaluated client scalability up to 100 participant clients across three benchmark NIDS datasets (UNSW-NB15, USTC-TFC2016, CIC-IDS-2017)
Achieved up to 3.6X training acceleration, 2.85X inference acceleration, and 90% model size reduction with ~99% accuracy
methodology: Base Classifiers / Feature Extractors: 2D CNNs (ResNet-50, ResNet-101, VGG-19) with a fully connected SoftMax classifier
Traffic Representation: Raw packets converted into 3-channel flow images using NFStream (300 bytes per packet × 40 packets per flow)
Pruning Method: Zero-shot structured pruning using DepGraph (L1-norm group importance scoring based on inter-layer and intra-layer dependencies) to generate a binary pruning mask tensor
FL Aggregation & Protocol: Centralized FL using FedAvg (benchmarked against FedProx) over 5 global communication rounds, 10 local client epochs, learning rate = 2 × 10⁻⁴
keyAssumptions: The global server is trusted to compute the mask and aggregate updates without altering model integrity
Clients share an identical feature space (Horizontal FL)
The zero-shot pruning mask computed at initialization on the server accurately reflects general parameter importance without requiring client data
Secure communication channels exist between the server and clients
datasets: CIC-IDS-2017: 14 attack classes + benign; 80 features extracted from PCAP
UNSW-NB15: 9 attack classes + benign; 49 features / PCAP
USTC-TFC2016: 10 malware traffic types + 10 normal traffic types
partition: IID: Normal and attack samples are evenly and proportionally split among all participant NIDS clients (the only scheme evaluated)
experimentalSetup: Hardware: African Super-Computing Center (UM6P) HPC node with 4 × NVIDIA A100 SXM4 80GB GPUs
Software: Python 3.9.15, PyTorch, Torch-Pruning (DepGraph), NFStream, NumPy, Pandas

Settings: 70% train / 30% test split; 5 global communication rounds; 10 local epochs; learning rate = 2 × 10⁻⁴; sparsity levels = 0%, 50%, 70%, 90%; 50% of clients randomly selected per round for aggregation
baselines: Unpruned federated learning baseline models (0% sparsity)
State-of-the-art FL-IDS models: MT-DNN-FL (Zhao et al. 2019), AFL (Agrawal et al. 2021), FedACNN (Man et al. 2021)
xaiEvaluation: N/A (no explainability method implemented or evaluated)
results: Accuracy stays around 99% across datasets and client counts even at high pruning rates (e.g., ResNet-50 at 70% sparsity reaches 99.94% on CIC-IDS-2017). Up to 3.62X training acceleration and 2.85X inference acceleration (VGG-19 at 90% sparsity on CIC-IDS-2017 with 50 users), and up to 90% model size reduction. FedAvg matched or surpassed FedProx in accuracy and training time at all tested sparsity levels.
failureConditions: At extreme sparsity (90%) on smaller or imbalanced datasets such as UNSW-NB15, accuracy dropped to 50% for ResNet-50 and VGG-19, due to lack of samples and extreme parameter pruning
High sparsity causes early-round performance fluctuations before stabilizing by round 5
costEvaluation: Measured training and inference acceleration ratios across 10, 50, and 100 clients, with up to 90% model size reduction and FLOPs reduction through sparse execution (Torch-Pruning / DepGraph). Exact network transmission bytes per round were not reported.

limitations.text: Evaluated only under IID data distributions; non-IID class skew across clients was not tested empirically. (Authors)
Did not evaluate defenses against poisoning attacks (data/model poisoning) or honest-but-curious server inference. (Authors)
Not deployed on physical low-end edge hardware; evaluated in a simulated GPU-based environment. (Authors)
Uses complex pruned deep CNNs (ResNet/VGG) without feature attribution methods (e.g., SHAP/LIME) for security analysts.
Does not measure exact network bandwidth transmission bytes per round across gRPC/socket channels.

futureWork: Address non-IID data distributions to improve performance and convergence in heterogeneous environments
Tackle privacy and security issues such as poisoning attacks and honest-but-curious servers
Adapt Lightweight-Fed-NIDS to Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and Operational Technology (OT) environments
relevance: Crucial benchmark for lightweight FL, model pruning and compression for edge IDS, or CNN-based intrusion detection on UNSW-NB15, USTC-TFC2016, and CIC-IDS-2017.
newIdeas: Non-IID robust and pruned FL-IDS: combine zero-shot structured pruning with non-IID FL algorithms (FedProx, pFedMe, SCAFFOLD) to prevent accuracy degradation under extreme data skew
XAI on pruned CNN features: apply SHAP / LIME to the 3-channel traffic image representations to explain which packet bytes drive intrusion alerts in pruned models
Poisoning-resilient pruned FL: combine zero-shot pruning with Byzantine-robust aggregation (Krum, Bulyan, Trimmed Mean) against malicious edge nodes
